newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam fetes anniversary of Russian revolution.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam fetes anniversary of Russian revolution.

text.p: Banner headlines in communist Vietnam's official newspapers on Thursday feted the 79th anniversary of Russia's "October Revolution" and the movement's leader, Vladimir Ilyich Lenin.

"The Great Stature and Effect of the October Revolution," the Communist Party daily Nhan Dan proclaimed over a grainy photograph of Lenin, whose Bolshevik followers overthrew the czarist government in November 6, 1917.
That date was October in Russia's old-style calendar.
Several other Vietnamese newspapers carried pictures of Lenin, whom historians consider a major force behind the founding of the now-defunct Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR).
"The October Revolution's ideal of peace, independence, democracy and socialism is still the compass for many nations to follow," the daily Hanoi Moi said.
"The Vietnamese and progressive people all over the world always look to the October Revolution, towards V.I. Lenin and the Soviet homeland with respect and deep gratitude," it added.

Vietnam's Communist Party, in a policy document published earlier this year, asserted that the collapse of the Soviet Union and Soviet bloc countries had driven socialism into only a "temporary regression".
Nhan Dan took up that theme, arguing that the October Revolution had opened "a transitional period from capitalism to socialism and communism across the whole globe".
Vietnam, one of five remaining communist-run countries, embarked on market-style reforms of its command economy and opened doors long closed to the outside world at the end of the 1980s.
However, some leaders fear that social changes brought by reform could undermine the Communist Party's grip on the country.

The official army newspaper Quan Doi Nhan Dan warned in a commentary on Monday that the party was under threat from imperialist forces seeking to sow disaffection among intellectuals, young people and the military.
